title: More Agents Is All You Need
authors: Junyou Li, Qin Zhang, Yangbin Yu, Qiang Fu, Deheng Ye
preview: Demonstrates that LLM performance scales with the number of agent instances via a simple sampling-and-voting method called Agent Forest, published at TMLR.
summary: Shows that instantiating multiple independent LLM agents and aggregating their outputs via majority voting (Agent Forest) improves performance across a wide range of benchmarks, with gains correlated to task difficulty. The method is orthogonal to and composable with existing prompt engineering and fine-tuning improvements. Comprehensive experiments confirm consistent scaling behaviour across model families and task types.
datacenter: Relevant to AI-on-iA and agentic serving infrastructure: Agent Forest implies that multi-agent workloads will require horizontally scalable head-node orchestration and efficient parallel inference capacity, with implications for request batching, load balancing, and CPU-side aggregation overhead at cluster scale.
metrics: Key result signal: performance scales consistently with agent count across benchmarks, with degree of improvement correlated to task difficulty.
